Chekitana shot three arrows at each great warrior, and each warrior shot seven arrows back at him.

Shikhandin, enraged, quickly took up a sword and a hundred-moon shield.
Shikhandin threw his sword at Chekitana's chariot, cutting Chekitana's bow and embedding itself in the ground.

The Pandavas were slaughtered by Satyaki on the battlefield, scattered and unable to fight calmly.
Satyaki stood on the battlefield after defeating the Pandavas led by Bhima, like a smokeless fire.
Great warriors were driven away by Satyaki under arrow showers and turned back.
Sanjaya narrated to King Dhritarashtra about the army being scattered by the great-souled Satyaki.
Satyaki, grandson of Shini, quickly charged toward Satyaki upon hearing the terrible shouts of Dhritarashtra's people in the great battle.

attributes.note: This appears to be a translation issue where both combatants are referred to as Satyaki. Based on context, this is Satyaki (Yuyudhana) attacking another warrior, possibly Kripa or another commander.

extraction_text: Satyaki, son of Hridika, showered sharp arrows at Satyaki, grandson of Shini, in great anger, making Satyaki furious.
Satyaki, grandson of Shini, shot a sharp crescent-headed arrow and four other arrows at Satyaki.
The four arrows killed Satyaki's horses, the crescent arrow cut his bow, and Satyaki killed his rear guard and charioteer with several arrows.
The truly heroic Satyaki made Satyaki lose his chariot and tormented his army with many straight arrows.
The army scattered under the arrows of Satyaki, grandson of Shini, and the truly heroic Satyaki took the opportunity to depart.
Sanjaya continued narrating to King Dhritarashtra about what this warrior did in his army, having crossed the ocean of Drona's army.
After defeating Satyaki in battle, the warrior was filled with joy and told his unflustered charioteer to go slowly.
Seeing Dhritarashtra's army filled with chariots, horses, elephants, and infantry, he spoke again to his charioteer.
He described the left side of Drona's army with a huge elephant force like a cloud, with golden chariots as leaders.
He noted these warriors were difficult to resist on the battlefield, following Duryodhana's orders to intercept him without fear of losing their lives.
He described the three-country noble chariot warriors with golden banners, facing him bravely and ready to fight.
He commanded his charioteer to immediately take him there so he could fight the three-country warriors in front of Drona.
The charioteer slowly proceeded according to the wish of Satyaki, descendant of the Shatvatas, with the chariot shining like the sun and banners gleaming.
The charioteer held the reins as the horses sped like wind on the battlefield, colored like jasmine, moon, and silver.
Seeing the conch-colored horses driving the chariot forward, heroes commanded the elephant army to surround this chariot, shooting various sharp arrows from all directions.
Satyaki, descendant of the Shatvatas, also shot countless arrows at the elephant army, like a huge cloud at summer's end raining on mountains.
The arrows shot by the Shini clan hero had the touch of a vajra, and the elephants couldn't endure the arrow torment, fleeing the battlefield.
The elephant army is in disarray with broken tusks, bleeding bodies, and dead riders.
King Jalasandha (Water-Connected) drives his elephant toward Satyaki's silver-horsed chariot.
